_note: Limits, not targets. Every number is a thin margin over a measurement taken on table.jonathanferwerda.com on 2026-11-01; see qa/README.md -> Budgets. A limit that can fail a run must say level: fail.

max_ms.why: one known slow page; a single route past 6 s is a finding

pss_peak_mb.why: past this a 4 GB box starts swapping, and the tree OOMs

cpu_peak_cores.why: table has 8 cores; a fan-out shows here

cpu_seconds.why: a full l1 smoke used ~120 s

rss_slope_mb_per_h.why: a soak that climbs faster than this leaks

db_failures.why: a broken schema or query plan is not a warning

ui_failures.why: a page that crashes the tree or 5xxes is a failure

pages_captured.why: below the eight pages the layer asks for

health_s.why: baseline 285 s (firstboot seeding); an installed disk answers in ~24 s

host_rss_mb.why: RSS is guest RAM + ~20 MB; run.sh gives the VM 3072 MB so the host needs ~3.1 GB

ux_failures.why: no baseline yet: until the nightly has a history, a note whose task failed is a finding, not a red run

duration_s.why: the UX loop has its own timer so a 20-minute run cannot hold the 04:00 l0-l2 job
